home.h1: One place and one API for all your retailers
home.lead: Open Brand Exchange is a free, open way to deliver your final product images and article data to your retailers. Your retailers get a portal with you, their software gets a standard API, and you publish automatically from your own systems.

steps.p: Have a provider run it, or host it yourself for free with one click or one command.
One CSV file and photos with a fixed name. Your PIM, ERP or a plain folder delivers them every night, with no manual work.

steps.h: Your retailers take it from there
steps.p: Retailers log in, paste their EAN list and download. Their software fetches the same content through the standard API.

what.h: Images, the way you meant them
what.p: Packshots, model shots and details, with their order, view, usage rights, embargo and whether AI was involved.
Style number, colour, EAN per size, season, description, material and care, in several languages.
A replaced packshot or a withdrawn image reaches your retailers by itself.

why.p: The standard and the software cost nothing. At most you pay for hosting, or for a provider if you prefer to outsource it.
Your content lives on your own server or with a provider you can leave. Every portal speaks the same language.
One publication for all your retailers. No more file transfers, emails with zips or a separate integration per store.

home.status: Open Brand Exchange is at the start. Version 0.2 of the specification and the software is out and free to use. We do not show customers or numbers that do not exist yet.

brands.labelNote: When something the law requires on the label is missing, such as the fibre composition or the materials of a shoe, Open Brand Exchange warns you at upload. A warning never blocks publishing.
brands.bagsNote: Luggage and bags now carry measurements (H × W × D, weight, volume) and features (wheels, lock, detachable strap …), measured the same way by every brand.
brands.startTitle: From your spreadsheet to every retailer, in four steps.

startSteps.p: An Excel file with the columns of the standard, drop-down lists for every fixed value and a filled-in example.
One row per size, by hand or exported from your own system. Name your photos style_colour_position, for example KO-1001_NVY_1.jpg.
Save as CSV UTF-8 and upload it in your portal with the photos, or let the portal fetch your export every night.
Your retailers find everything in your portal. Their software receives every change automatically. Free of charge.

brands.partnersP: A provider can take over the entire process. Photopilot, for example, offers a free portal with the OBX connection, full automation of the process and a custom integration with your ERP.

automation.lead: Your PIM, ERP, DAM or a shared folder already has the data and the photos. Pick the first recipe that fits: they work with every Open Brand Exchange portal.
head: You have…
Use
Code needed
rows: a CSV or zip on a web address, SFTP server or S3 bucket
a server or PC that runs nightly jobs
your exports in a Git repository
a developer who connects your PIM or ERP
automation.formatP: Every way of publishing reads the same thing: a products.csv with one row per size, and photos named {style}_{color}_{position}.jpg. Once you have that, every recipe below works.
automation.keyP: In your admin, go to Automatic upload → Access keys and create a new key. You then have two values: the address of your portal (OBX_URL) and the key itself (OBX_TOKEN). The key is shown only once.
automation.keyTip: Give every system its own key. Then you can revoke one without breaking the others.
automation.scheduledP: In your admin: Automatic upload → Scheduled imports → Add scheduled import. Choose the source and how often it runs.

scheduled.v: the address of a products.csv, or of a zip with products.csv and photos. Login details are stored encrypted.
server, user, password or key, and the folder with the export.
AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO or Backblaze: endpoint, bucket, folder and a read-only key.

automation.scheduledMode: Choose "Only add and update" or "Also take missing articles offline". The second also takes offline what disappeared from the file, but stops when more than half of a brand would disappear, so a broken export never empties your catalog. "Test connection" shows which files it would read.
automation.cliP: obx is a single program for Windows, macOS and Linux. It reads OBX_URL and OBX_TOKEN from the environment, uploads only new or changed photos, makes the web versions when needed and waits until your portal has processed everything. Run it as often as you like: unchanged articles cost nothing.
automation.cliExit: Exit code 0 = all good, 2 = done but some rows had errors (they are listed), 1 = failed.
automation.watchTitle: 2. A folder that publishes itself: obx watch
automation.watchP: Let your PIM, ERP or a colleague save exports into a folder. obx watch publishes whenever something changes and skips photos that stayed the same. Run it as a service, or with Docker:
automation.githubP: Store OBX_URL and OBX_TOKEN as repository secrets. The same works in GitLab CI, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps: install obx and run obx push.
automation.httpP: Use a plain HTTP Request step with the header Authorization: Bearer followed by your key. Every step is safe to repeat: sending the same data twice changes nothing.
automation.httpProduct: Article (for example when it changes in your PIM)
automation.httpVariant: Colour and size, with its EAN
automation.httpImage: Photo: first the details, then the file itself
automation.httpImageNote: The Portal for Cloudflare does not make web versions of photos itself. Publish with obx or with "Imports" in your admin there: they make them for you. Photos that arrive another way, such as from a scheduled import, are shown in their original size until then.
automation.httpHooks: Want a signal when something happens? In your admin, add a notification (webhook) for a finished import or a new access request, and let it start an n8n, Make or Zapier trigger.
automation.apiP: An integration remembers what it sent last time and sends only the changes, in batches. Or send the CSV as it is and let the portal read it.
automation.apiBatch: Skip photos the portal already has, then send one batch
automation.apiImport: A CSV and a zip of photos in one go
automation.apiMore: Every detail is in the specification:

hosting.lead: One portal is one brand company on one server. You choose how to run it, from fully outsourced to fully yourself. Below, from simplest to most hands-on.
hosting.p1Title: 3. A partner hosts it for you
hosting.p1P: Rather not host it yourself? Partners can host and maintain the portal for you.
hosting.listP: The criteria for a listing here are the same for everyone:
listItems: your portal passes the conformance test for the current version
a brand can export all its data and images and leave
you publish your own prices and terms on your own site
hosting.listHow: Being compatible is free; a listing here is part of the official partnership.
hosting.p2P: Your own portal on your own account, without managing a server.
hosting.cfP: Runs on Cloudflare Workers, with D1 as the database and R2 for the images. Click the button, sign in to Cloudflare and follow the steps. A portal in daily use needs the Workers Paid plan (5 dollars a month); the free plan is only enough to look around. Web versions of your photos are made by your browser and the obx tool.
hosting.runP: A script that puts your portal on Google Cloud Run. You need a Google Cloud account and the gcloud tool.
hosting.phpP: For the web hosting package you may already have, with PHP and a database. No commands needed:
phpSteps: Download obx-portal-php-<version>.zip from the latest release.
Unzip it and upload the folder to your hosting with (S)FTP.
Point your (sub)domain, for example brands.yourbrand.com, at the folder called public.
Make the folders data and config writable (permissions 775; if the installer still says they are not, 777).
Open that address. The installer checks your server and asks for the setup code from the file data/SETUP-CODE.txt, which you open with your FTP program. Then click “Open the setup wizard”.
Add the cron address the installer shows as a cron job in your hosting control panel, every 5 minutes. Without it the portal still works.
hosting.p3P: On your own server or on any cloud that runs containers. One command:
hosting.composeP: Or with HTTPS included, through Caddy:
hosting.envPublicUrl: the public address of your portal
hosting.envSecretKey: a long random key (openssl rand -hex 32); keep it safe
hosting.envSetupCode: optional: a setup code you choose in advance
first: Open the address of your portal in your browser.

Enter the one-time setup code. It is in the log on the first start (Portal for web hosting: in data/SETUP-CODE.txt, and the installer fills it in for you), or you set it in advance with OBX_SETUP_CODE.
Fill in your company and your first brand, and choose your own password. There is never a default password.
hosting.firstWhy: The setup code makes sure nobody else can claim a freshly installed portal.
hosting.domainP: Use a subdomain such as brands.yourbrand.com or b2b.yourbrand.com. Retailers then see your name, and your address stays the same when you change hosting.
hosting.compareP: The three editions do the same thing and have the same admin and retailer portal. Choose what fits your hosting; you can switch later.
hosting.heroLead: The software is free. You choose where it runs, and you can move at any time.
heroChecks: Free software, you only pay for hosting
Recommended: in Europe, for example with Hetzner (Germany)
The same portal everywhere, so you can always switch
Prefer not to do it yourself? A partner hosts it for you
hosting.euP: A small server at a European provider is enough for most brands. The guide below uses Hetzner, with data centres in Germany and Finland. Any server that runs Docker works the same way.
euSteps: Create a server at Hetzner in Nuremberg, Falkenstein or Helsinki, with backups switched on.
Point your domain, for example images.yourbrand.com, at the server.
Install Docker and start the portal with one command. HTTPS is arranged automatically.
Open your domain and complete the setup wizard.
Optional: keep the images in Hetzner Object Storage, in the same location.
Schedule a nightly backup. Updates are one command.
hosting.euGuide: Step-by-step guide: your portal on Hetzner
hosting.euData: With the server and storage in an EU location, your catalog, images and database are stored in the EU.
hosting.webP: The PHP edition runs on ordinary European web hosting with PHP and a database, for example at TransIP, Strato or OVHcloud. No commands needed:
hosting.altP: The same portal also runs on Cloudflare Workers and on Google Cloud Run. Choose a region in Europe where the service offers one.

retailers.toolsP: Open Brand Exchange is an open standard that any software can support. Photopilot is building it into its software for retailers. Other vendors can do the same. No specific software is required: a browser is sufficient.
retailers.findP: Brands that choose to be listed appear in the directory. A brand can also give you the address of its portal directly.
retailers.kitTitle: If a brand does not participate yet, send this email

retailers.kitMore: More material, such as the brochure for retailers, is on the downloads page.

label.title: Care label information is included with every article.
label.p: Composition per part, care instructions in label order and the country of origin are part of every article, next to the EAN of each size. Your shop can display them as text or as care symbols in its own style. The fields follow the EU textile labelling rules and the ISO 3758 care codes, so they can also feed a digital product passport later.

switchKit.subject: Your product images and article data through Open Brand Exchange?
switchKit.body:
Dear [name],

We sell [brand] in our store and online shop. To present your articles well, we need your final product photos and article data: the EAN per size, material, care instructions and the images in the right order.

Today this often reaches us as loose files and emails. Would you consider Open Brand Exchange? It is a free, open standard that lets a brand publish its content once for all of its retailers:

- your own portal where we log in, search by our EANs and download;
- a standard API, so our software fetches images and data by itself;
- automatic publishing from your PIM, ERP or a folder of exports.

The software is open source: you can host it yourself for free or choose a provider. You decide who gets access and you see who downloads what.

More information: {url}

Kind regards,

[name]
[store]
[city]

developers.lead: Open Brand Exchange is a specification with three APIs, JSON Schemas, test data and a conformance suite. The specification is the source of truth; the implementations follow it.

items.a: The standard and the software are free. If you host it yourself you pay only for your hosting. A provider charges its own prices, which you find on its own website.

Not for the basics. You can install a portal with one click, and a scheduled import from a web address, SFTP server or bucket needs no code. A developer helps if you want to connect your PIM or ERP directly.

items.q: Is this another platform we have to join?
items.a: No. Every brand runs its own portal, on its own domain if it likes. There is no central platform that holds your content.

items.q: Who decides which retailer gets access?
items.a: You do. Retailers request access, and you approve or reject each request. You can also choose which brands a retailer sees and whether originals may be downloaded.
A browser. Retailers with software that fetches images by itself can request an API key for that software.
The original, exactly as you uploaded it, plus a web version (at most 2000 px), a square version and a small preview. Retailers choose what they need.

items.q: Does it keep information about AI and rights in the images?
items.a: Yes. Usage rights, the embargo date and whether AI was involved are part of every image. Originals are stored and delivered unchanged, including any embedded content credentials.
Yes. Every portal speaks the same standard and every provider listed here lets you export all your content. Your own domain stays the same.
Yes, version 0.2: the specification, the three portals, the obx command and the conformance check are released and free to use. It is early days: the first brands are joining now.

Open Brand Exchange is being handed over to the {foundation}, a Dutch non-profit foundation (stichting), so that the standard belongs to the brands, retailers and software vendors who use it, not to one company. Questions go to {email}.

items.q: How is this different from closed content platforms?
items.a: Closed platforms keep the brands' content in one company's system and charge brands or retailers for access. Open Brand Exchange is an open standard: each brand runs its own portal or chooses a provider, and can export everything and leave. Any software can implement it without a licence fee.

items.q: Can our image portal or DAM connect?
items.a: Yes. An image portal, image bank or DAM that offers the read side of the protocol and passes the conformance test is compatible. Retailers' software then fetches its product images, per article and EAN, the same way as from any brand portal.

governance.lead: Open Brand Exchange should belong to the brands, retailers and software vendors who use it, not to one company.

sections.p: Until there are three independent implementations that pass the conformance suite, the founder decides on changes, after public discussion. After that, a steering group takes over, with one seat per implementer and at least one brand and one retailer.

Every change to the standard is a public pull request with a short reason. Larger proposals stay open for comments for at least 14 days. Anyone can contribute, without signing a contributor agreement.

Nothing in the standard may require a particular vendor or hosted service. Anyone may implement it, host it for others or build a competing product on it. No implementation gets special treatment in the conformance suite, including that of Photopilot, the initiator's company.

The specification and the content of this site are CC-BY-4.0. The SDK, the obx tool and the shared web interface are Apache-2.0. The three portal editions are AGPL-3.0, so improvements to them stay open. The code of this site is MIT.

governance.nameP: The name "Open Brand Exchange" is the same in every language and is never translated. It is not a registered trademark yet. Software that passes the conformance test may say it is "Compatible with Open Brand Exchange".
governance.foundationP: The {foundation} is being set up as a Dutch foundation (stichting). Once it exists, the copyright, the name, the domain and the GitHub organisation will be transferred to it.

privacy.lead: This website does not track you. Below is what little data is processed, and why.

sections.p: Until the foundation is registered, the controller for this website is {publisher}, the sole proprietorship of {person}, on behalf of the {foundation} (address and registration number in the imprint). For anything about privacy, email {email}.
Nothing that identifies you. This site has no forms, no accounts, no newsletter and no cookies.

The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages. Like every web server, Cloudflare processes technical data such as your IP address to deliver the pages and protect them against abuse. We keep no access logs ourselves.
If visitor statistics are switched on, we use Cloudflare Web Analytics. It counts page views without cookies and without following you across sites. We only see totals.
If you email us, we use your address and message only to answer you, and delete them once they are no longer needed for that.
You may ask what personal data we have about you, and have it corrected or deleted. You may also complain to the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).
Every brand portal is run by the brand itself or its provider. Their privacy statement applies there, not this one.

imprint.lead: Who publishes this website, and how to reach us.
imprint.foundationP: Open Brand Exchange is published by {publisher} on behalf of the {foundation}, which is being set up as a Dutch foundation (stichting). {publisher} is the sole proprietorship of {person}.
imprint.securityNote: Please report vulnerabilities privately to this address, not in a public issue.
imprint.contentP: We write this site with care, but it may contain mistakes. For technical details, the specification is authoritative. The texts may be reused under CC BY 4.0 with attribution; the code of this site is MIT-licensed.

sections.p: We use no cookies for statistics, advertising or anything else, so we do not ask for your consent either.

If you pick a language, your browser remembers it in its own storage (localStorage), so your next visit opens in that language. It is never sent to us. Clearing this site's data in your browser removes it.
Only if Cloudflare, our host, has to check that a visitor is not an automated attack, it may set a strictly necessary security cookie for that check. It is not used for anything else.
Brand portals are separate websites, run by the brand or its provider. Their own cookie statement applies there.

home.h1: The standard for brands and retailers.
home.lead: One way to share product photos and article data: in a portal, as a download, or straight into the retailer's software.
home.videoNote: Captioned, so it can be followed without sound.
home.flowTitle: When every party structures data the same way, every party benefits.
home.flowLead: At almost every retailer, someone copies spreadsheets and retypes product data for each brand, under time pressure with every new collection. A shared standard removes that work. It is implemented once and benefits every party for years. Time for better work.
home.flowCaption: What a brand puts in, the open standard in the middle, and what retailers get out.

inItems: Product data from PIM, ERP or Excel
flow.stdLead: One fixed structure for every brand

items: A full copy first, then only the changes

home.trustTitle: An open standard, not a platform.
home.trustLead: Open Brand Exchange is intended to belong to the brands, retailers and software vendors that use it, not to a single company.

trust.p: Version 0.2, under CC-BY-4.0. Anyone may implement it, including for commercial use.
A brand can export all its data and images at any time, move to another provider or host it itself.
The SDK, the obx tool and the web interface are Apache-2.0. The three portal editions are AGPL-3.0, so improvements stay open.
The copyright, the name and the domain go to the {foundation} once it is registered.
This website sets no cookies, uses no trackers and loads nothing from other servers.

partners.h1: Compatible for free. Listed as an official partner.
partners.lead: Any portal, image portal, PIM, ERP or provider can work with Open Brand Exchange. The test and the label “Compatible with Open Brand Exchange” are free. A listing as official partner is a paid membership, with the same criteria for everyone.

partners.testP: The conformance test is open source. Run it against your own portal as often as you like. It checks discovery, the change feed, products, images and security, and says in plain language what is still missing.
testSteps: Load the fictional test brand Kestrel into a test account of your portal.
Run obx-conformance against your portal, as described in the developer guide.
Fix what fails, until the result says CONFORMANT.
partners.certP: Send us the JSON report and the address of your test portal. We run the same test and confirm the result. From then on you may say your product is “Compatible with Open Brand Exchange”, for the version you tested.
partners.partnerP: Official partners are listed with their logo on the partner and hosting pages, carry the “Official partner” badge and are named to brands that ask us for a provider.

meta.title: Online compatibility check
meta.description: Check a portal from the outside against the Open Brand Exchange protocol tests. Read-only: the check never writes to your portal.

check.linkLead: Want a quick first look? The online compatibility check tests a portal from the outside, read-only.
check.lead: Enter the address of a portal and see which parts of the OBX protocol tests it passes. It takes about a minute.
about: It runs the parts of the OBX protocol tests that can run from the outside, against the address you enter.
It only reads. It never writes to the portal, never changes data and never sends notifications.
Without a key it checks discovery, sign-in and error answers. With a test API key it also reads products, the change feed and images.
Tests that write to the portal or need steps by the brand only run in the full conformance test, obx-conformance, on your own machine.
check.fullRun: How to run the full conformance test
check.urlHint: The address of the portal, starting with https://
check.urlInvalid: Enter the address of the portal, starting with https://
check.keyHint: With a key more checks run. Use a test key and revoke it afterwards.
check.keyIncomplete: Enter both the client id and the client secret, or leave both empty.
check.robotLabel: Check that you are a person
check.robotMissing: Wait until the check that you are a person is done, then try again.
check.robotFailed: The check that you are a person could not load. Reload the page and try again.
check.noscript: This check needs JavaScript. You can also run the full conformance test on your own machine.

errors.invalid_url: This is not a valid address. Enter the address of the portal, starting with https://
errors.not_https: The address must start with https://. The check only talks to portals over a secure connection.
errors.ip_address: Enter the domain name of the portal, not an IP address.
errors.port: Use the standard port: the address cannot contain a port number.
errors.not_public: This address is not reachable from the internet. The online check only tests public portals.
errors.dns: This domain name could not be found. Check the address for typos.
errors.bad_client: The client id or client secret is not in a valid format.
errors.bad_request: The request was not valid. Reload the page and try again.
errors.turnstile: The check that you are a person failed or expired. Try again.
errors.rate_limited: You have started many checks in a short time. Please wait a while.
errors.busy: This portal is being checked right now. Try again when that check is done.
errors.cooldown: This portal was checked in the last 10 minutes. Wait a little before you check it again.
errors.daily_cap: The online check has reached its limit for today. Try again tomorrow, or run obx-conformance on your own machine.
errors.unavailable: The online check is not available right now. Try again later.
errors.internal: The check stopped because of an error on our side. Try again later.
errors.not_found: This result was not found. Shared results are kept for 30 days.
errors.network: The check could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.

check.partial: Passed, but only part of this check can run online.

tiers.local: Only runs locally, with obx-conformance: these tests write to the portal or need steps by the brand.
tiers.fixtures: Needs a test account with the Kestrel test data (or a second test key).

check.summaryPassP: Every check that ran online passed: {passed} passed, {skipped} not checked online. This is not the full conformance test.
check.summaryNotChecked: Not checked online (needs a test API key or test data)
check.summaryFailP: Open a failed check below to see what went wrong.
check.setupTitle: The check could not start properly
check.setupKey: The test API key does not work: the portal refused the client id or client secret. Check the key, or leave it empty to run the checks without a key.
check.setupOther: Something needed before the tests could not be done. The message of the test tool:
check.noDiscovery: No OBX discovery document found at {url}. This address does not look like an OBX portal.
check.shareP: The link is valid for 30 days.
check.storedP: A stored result. The link is valid until {date}.

tests.P-DISC-1: The portal publishes its discovery document at /.well-known/obx, public and in the right format, so software can find its API.
tests.P-DISC-2: The portal offers the required functions (change feed, products, lookup by barcode, image files) and answers clearly for optional functions it does not offer.
tests.P-AUTH-1: Software can sign in with a client id and secret; a wrong secret or an unknown permission is refused with the right error.
tests.P-AUTH-2: Requests without a valid key are refused, and a key the brand has revoked stops working at once.
tests.P-AUTH-3: A retailer without permission for original files never sees or receives an original image.
tests.P-ACC-1: A retailer can request access, follow the request, and receives its key exactly once after the brand approves.
tests.P-FEED-1: The change feed starts with exactly the products and images this retailer may see, in a fixed order.
tests.P-FEED-2: Paging through the change feed gives the same result with small and large pages: nothing is skipped or repeated.
tests.P-FEED-3: An invalid position in the change feed is refused with a clear error.
tests.P-FEED-4: A retailer that may only see one brand sees only that brand's products and images, everywhere.
tests.P-FEED-5: Data the brand imports leads to exactly the expected changes for retailers.
tests.P-FEED-6: When the brand changes what a retailer may see, the retailer is told to fetch everything again.
tests.P-CAT-1: Two test products come out with exactly the expected article data.
tests.P-CAT-2: The product list pages through all products completely and stably, and lookup by id works.
tests.P-CAT-3: Looking up products by barcode (EAN) gives the expected answer; too many codes at once are refused.
tests.P-CAT-4: Products a retailer may not see answer “not found”, so their existence is not revealed.
tests.P-CAT-5: Test products for luggage, bags and shoes come out with exactly the expected article data: materials, measurements, features and certifications.
tests.P-CAT-6: Every product has the article data of version 0.2 in the right shape, with the right names for materials and care symbols.
tests.P-MEDIA-1: The test images carry the expected information, such as AI provenance, embargo dates and the absence of an original.
tests.P-MEDIA-2: Every image file matches its checksum and supports caching, partial downloads and temporary links.
tests.P-MEDIA-3: Original files are delivered unchanged; web and thumbnail versions have the right size and format and are never enlarged.
tests.P-ERR-1: Every error answer has the standard format with a known error code, so software can handle it.
tests.P-RATE-1: The portal tells software its request limits, and says when to retry after too many requests.
tests.P-EXP-1: A full export (a zip file with a list of files and checksums) is complete and correct.
tests.P-HOOK-1: The portal sends signed notifications (webhooks) and refuses unsafe destinations.
tests.P-USE-1: The portal accepts usage reports from retailers and counts them.
